# Pane termination cards: RED contract for #1933

`inbox-termination-cards.json` supplies the seven cases to `inbox/status/008` in `tests/render_dashboard.rs` and `desktop/src/components/InboxSurfaces.test.tsx`. Desired user words live in `inbox-display.json` under `cardTerminations`; they are the existing `terminations` explanations prefixed with `not delivered: `. The desired TestBackend snapshots are generated from those words and checked separately against cards rendered from the real hub's notice, so snapshot acceptance cannot approve the old fixed notices.

Each case's `cardNotice` is a capture of today's daemon-authored delivery-notice string, verified against the real `InboxHub` sink by the Rust test before the desktop tests consume it through the existing error-event and snapshot paths. Refresh these captured strings when implementing the producer fix. Changing the captures alone fails the Rust producer check; leaving them unchanged keeps the desktop tests RED. This contract does not require a new desktop event path or new protocol fields.

The seven cases are deck-attributed exit 0, deck-attributed exit 7, connection ended, replaced, closed, unknown, and wrapper-attributed exit 23 followed by a close settlement. The last case pins retention after the hub's natural-exit settlement, not the earlier PTY race or correctness of wrapper attribution; `inbox/status/032` covers those production mechanisms.

The isolated Rust test fails with `termination wording missing from cards:` and lists the seven actual grids. For example, the exit-seven card expects `not delivered: the command started in the agent's pane exited (code 7) before taking this message`, but renders `not delivered: the command started in this agent's pane exited before a deck message reached it`. Replaced and closed both render `not delivered: this agent's pane ended before a deck message reached it`, losing their distinction. Desired snapshots were reviewed for the full explanation, codes 0/7/23, connection uncertainty, the previous-agent distinction, and visible Error status at 180 columns.

The desktop file has 14 expected failures (seven streamed notices and seven hydrated notices), each an `expect(element).toHaveTextContent()` mismatch showing the same captured fixed string; its other 52 tests pass. The existing `InboxAttention.test.tsx` test `uses exactly the shared words` also fails because production `INBOX_WORDS` has not yet acquired `cardTerminations`. That is part of the requested shared-words implementation, not a snapshot to accept or a parity assertion to weaken.

Covering commands are `rwx sandbox exec -- cargo test-fast --test render_dashboard status_008_card_shows_not_delivered_error_notice`, `rwx sandbox exec -- cargo test-fast --no-fail-fast`, `pnpm test src/components/InboxSurfaces.test.tsx`, and `pnpm test src/components/InboxAttention.test.tsx src/lib/inboxWords.test.ts src/lib/daemonEvents.test.ts` from `desktop/`. Formatting and four-flag clippy remain required before committing this intentionally failing test slice.

Validation on 2026-10-31, based on part-3 commit `fb941016`: `cargo fmt --check` passed locally; four-flag clippy, linkage-check (18 rules) and `cargo xtask docs --tests` passed in RWX. The full workspace fast suite ran 9,205 tests: 9,204 passed and only `status_008_card_shows_not_delivered_error_notice` failed as requested, with seven existing tests skipped. Desktop results were 52 passing / 14 expected failing in `InboxSurfaces.test.tsx`, and 38 passing / one expected parity failure across `InboxAttention.test.tsx`, `inboxWords.test.ts` and `daemonEvents.test.ts`; `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passed. Production code was unchanged; these tests exercised no real agent or production daemon, and no lane-2 test was run.
